title: Start here: crypto for beginners
h1: Start here: crypto for complete beginners
seo_title: Start here: crypto for complete beginners
description: A plain-English beginner path: what crypto is, how to buy safely, how to set up a wallet, your first trades, the 10 biggest mistakes, and how to avoid losses.
summary: Six short steps from zero to your first safe trade.
plain: New to crypto? Read these six steps in order. Each one takes a few minutes and links to a deeper guide when you're ready. Unfamiliar words are explained in the glossary.
dont_lose: Only invest what you can afford to lose.
risk: Not financial advice; no strategy wins every trade.

sections.title: Step 1: What crypto is, in two minutes

paras: A cryptocurrency is digital money recorded on a blockchain, a public ledger that thousands of computers keep in sync. Nobody can change it alone. Bitcoin was the first. Ethereum and Solana let people build apps and new tokens on top.
There are thousands of coins. Most are speculative and many go to zero. Start by learning, not by buying.

items: Use a large, regulated exchange in your country
Type its address yourself, or use the official app store. Never use an ad or a link from a message.
Lock the account
Turn on an authenticator app or a security key, not SMS, and use a unique password.
Start tiny
Make a small first purchase and a small test withdrawal before moving real money.
Keep records
Save each purchase for taxes. A tax tool can import them later.

paras: Install a well-known wallet app from its official site, write the seed phrase on paper, and store it somewhere safe and offline. Once you hold amounts you'd hate to lose, get a hardware wallet direct from the maker.

items: Swap a tiny amount first
Try a $5-10 swap to learn how fees, slippage and confirmations work.
Decide your exit before you buy
Write down where you'll take profit and where you'll cut the loss.
Risk 1-2% per trade
That way one bad trade can't hurt you much.
Check the coin first
Run token-safety checks before buying anything new.
1. Sharing your seed phrase
No real exchange, wallet or support agent will ever ask for it. Anyone who does is a scammer.
2. Investing money you need
Crypto can fall 50-90%. Only use money you could lose without it changing your life.
3. Chasing green candles
Buying after a huge jump usually means buying from people who are taking profit.
4. Trusting DMs and 'support'
Unsolicited messages offering help, jobs or investments are almost always scams.
5. Clicking airdrop and claim links
Fake claim pages drain wallets. Use only links from the project's official site.
6. Using leverage early
Leverage multiplies losses, and liquidation can take everything in minutes.
7. Keeping everything on one exchange or one hot wallet
Exchanges fail and hot wallets get drained. Split your money, and keep savings in cold storage.
8. Ignoring fees
Fees, slippage and spreads quietly eat small accounts, especially when you trade often.
9. Believing guaranteed returns
Fixed high 'daily returns' are the classic sign of a Ponzi scheme.
10. Not writing anything down
Without notes on your trades and taxes, you can't learn from your mistakes or file correctly.

paras: Read the scam guide once. Most losses come from a handful of repeated tricks. Use a burner wallet for anything new, and revoke old approvals every month. If something feels urgent, stop: urgency is the scammer's main tool.
